Senses.PreferredTarget: the further matter beyond what has been reached
Senses.Explanation: Toward or facing (向), above or further up (上), and matter or affair (事): the further matter beyond what has already been reached or named. It runs in a recurrent dialogue. A monk asks whether there is still an upward matter (向上還有事也無／還有向上事也無); the respondent says yes; the monk asks, 'What is the upward matter?' (如何是向上事); and the respondent gives an answer such as 'break the mirror and come; I will meet you' (打破鏡來，與汝相見), 'a person from Silla does not wrap his head' (新羅人不褁頭), or 'downward the text runs long' (向下文長). It also appears in 'knows that there is an upward matter' (知有向上事, 69 occurrences) and its negation. One line says that Xuefeng had words only after he knew there was an upward matter (雪峯知有向上事始有語話分). The expression can be dismissed with 'What upward matter are you talking about?' (說甚麼向上事). The corpus also attaches 'upward' to named limits: 'the matter upward from buddha' (佛向上事, 169 occurrences) and 'upward from Vairocana' (毘盧向上). It is paired with 'the last word' (末後句) in the statement that one must also know the upward matter and the last word (更須知有向上事末後句始得). Related forms include 'the upward road' (向上一路, 1,082), 'the upward move' (向上一著, 303), 'the upward aperture' (向上一竅, 292), 'the upward pivot' (向上關捩子, 62), 'the upward person' (向上人, 253), and 'the upward vehicle of the lineage' (向上宗乘, 491). Yuanwu Keqin states directly that an upward person must know the upward matter, providing an independent own-record witness for the same relational formulation.
Senses.Note: A corpus-wide term, with 1,363 hits in 222 allowlist texts. The full dialogue—whether there is an upward matter, yes, then what it is—recurs across houses. The word 'upward' (向上) is relative to whatever the text has just named, as shown by 'the matter beyond Buddha' (佛向上事) and 'beyond Vairocana' (毘盧向上).

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰。如何是向上事。師曰。打破鏡來。與汝相見。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), Lingyun Zhiqin section. Changsheng Jiaoran remains the named exact questioner through the complete exchange and asks what the upward matter is; Lingyun answers, 'break the mirror and come; I will meet you.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 此人還知有向上事也無。師曰。不知。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Zhaozhou Congshen section. An unnamed questioner asks whether this person knows there is an upward matter; Zhaozhou answers, 'does not know.' The six-rung ladder does not name the questioner.

Occurrences.Kwic: 更須知有向上事末後句始得
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of the Ancient Worthies (古尊宿語錄), Foyan Qingyuan's recorded sayings. Foyan Qingyuan is the exact speaker: in his hall address he says that even after seeing colors clearly one must know the matter beyond and the final phrase before study is finished.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧云向上還有事也無師云有僧云如何是向上事師云新羅人不褁頭
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), in Shoushan Xingnian's section. An unnamed monk is the exact speaker who asks whether there is an upward matter and then asks what the upward matter is; Shoushan answers first 'yes' and then 'a person from Silla does not wrap his head.' The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, exact full-case search, and parallel passages do not name this monk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問如何是向上事師云向下文長
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), in Muzhou Daoming's section. An unnamed monk is the exact speaker asking the headword question; Muzhou answers. The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel passage do not name the monk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉洞山云須知有佛向上事僧問如何是佛向上事山云非佛
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of the Ancient Worthies (古尊宿語錄), Yunmen Wenyan's recorded sayings: Yunmen raises Dongshan Liangjie's statement that one must know the matter beyond buddha; Dongshan Liangjie is the exact quoted utterer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不識善惡。說甚麼向上事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Zhaozhou Congshen section: Zhaozhou Congshen dismisses the premise by asking what upward matter can be spoken of.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：「還有向上事也無？」師云：「有。」進云：「如何是向上事？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The cited recorded-sayings collection (入就瑞白禪師語錄): an unnamed monk asks Ruibai Mingxue whether there is still an upward matter and then what that matter is; all six attribution rungs leave the questioner unnamed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師舉僧問雪峯知有向上事始有語話分時如何峯提起僧手云作麼生

ActorAttribution.ActorLabel: unnamed monk in the raised Xuefeng case

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of the Ancient Worthies (古尊宿語錄), Foyan Qingyuan's recorded sayings: an unnamed monk in the case asks Xuefeng Yicun about having speech only after knowing the upward matter; Foyan later raises the case, and all six attribution rungs leave the original monk unnamed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若是向上人。須知向上事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄): Yuanwu Keqin says that an upward person must know the upward matter.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 須知更有向上一竅在。作麼生是向上一竅？
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: 入就瑞白禪師語錄: Ruibai Mingxue says there is still an upward aperture and asks what it is.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 我今更踏向上一著，千聖俱立下風。
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: 隱元禪師語錄: Yinyuan Longqi says that he now takes the upward move, with the thousand sages standing downwind.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 所以道。向上一路千聖不傳。
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: 圓悟佛果禪師語錄: Yuanwu Keqin raises the stock statement that the upward road is not transmitted by the thousand sages.
圓悟佛果禪師語錄: Yuanwu Keqin asks what it is like when an upward person comes.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 提持向上宗乘，更須颺卻全身向那邊更那邊翻箇筋斗
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: 神鼎雲外澤禪師語錄: Shending Yunwai Ze speaks of upholding the upward vehicle of the lineage and turning a somersault beyond the whole body.
天界覺浪盛禪師語錄: Juelang Daosheng says that the upward pivot is not yet known.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 毘盧向上未聞此等風規。
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: 天目中峰廣錄: Zhongfeng Mingben says that above Vairocana such customs have not been heard of.
